evals.prompt: I run a small SaaS doing about $4k MRR and I've got Mixpanel, GA4 and Hotjar but honestly I still don't know what's actually moving the needle. What should I be tracking every week?
evals.expected_output: Recognises a metrics/analytics request. Recommends a north star (revenue/MRR) plus 2-4 input metrics, a metric tree, and a single activation event, and pushes back on the tool sprawl ('42 metrics, learning nothing'). Produces a metrics spec in founder/metrics/ and a weekly digest cadence rather than another dashboard.
expectations: Defaults the north star to revenue / MRR and names 2-4 input metrics
Rejects the many-tools/many-metrics sprawl and cuts to the few numbers that change decisions
Defines one specific activation event rather than using signup
Points to founder/metrics/ outputs and the weekly digest script

evals.expected_output: Writes the CSV to founder/metrics/metrics.csv and runs scripts/weekly_digest.py. Reports the digest with period-over-period deltas, flags the adverse movers (churned_mrr and failed_payments_mrr spiking, new_customers down), splits the involuntary churn share from failed_payments_mrr / churned_mrr, and ends with exactly ONE recommended action.
expectations: Runs the digest script on the CSV rather than eyeballing the numbers
Treats churn / failed payments as good-when-down and ranks them as adverse movers
Reports the inferred involuntary-churn share from failed_payments_mrr
Ends in exactly one recommended action, not a list of observations

evals.prompt: our churn went from 4% to 6% this month and we're panicking. customers keep saying 'too expensive' on the cancel survey. what do we do?
evals.expected_output: Reframes churn as often an activation problem ('most churn happens before value'), insists on splitting voluntary vs involuntary churn (failed cards are commonly 20-40% of total), checks the dunning setup and recovery rate, reads the retention cohort curve, and defines an activation event. Recommends one action via the theory of constraints, not a scattergun of retention tactics.
expectations: Splits churn into voluntary vs involuntary before proposing fixes
Calls out dunning / failed payments as the highest-ROI solo lever
Notes that most churn happens before value, so onboarding/activation comes first
Recommends exactly one action against the single binding constraint

evals.prompt: how do I actually pick an 'activation' metric for my tool? everyone online says just use signups and I'm not sure.
evals.expected_output: Explains that activation is not signup — it is the specific countable action that correlates with a user staying (Slack-style volume, Dropbox-style second device, Figma-style first files given only as illustrations, not copied numbers). Shows how to derive it from retained-vs-churned week-one behaviour, writes it as one sentence, and instruments it with time-to-value.
expectations: Describes the method for finding it (retained vs churned week-one behaviour) rather than hardcoding a number
Frames activation examples as illustrations to reason by analogy
Connects activation to time-to-value and the onboarding sequence
